title: Bumrah Finds Rhythm in Delhi Nets Ahead of Afghanistan T20I Return
excerpt: Bowling at full intensity in Thursday's Delhi nets, Jasprit Bumrah looked ready for his first T20I since March. Shreyas Iyer wants him to get game time; Afghanistan say they have a plan for him.
body:
• Jasprit Bumrah bowled at full intensity in the Delhi nets on Thursday, his strongest signal yet that he is ready for a T20I return after a left knee injury that has kept him out since July.
  • India captain Shreyas Iyer backed Bumrah's return ahead of the Afghanistan T20I series, stressing the importance of game time for a bowler coming back from injury.
  • The three-match series begins Sunday, September 13 at Arun Jaitley Stadium, with Afghanistan captain Ibrahim Zadran saying his side has specific plans ready for Bumrah.
  • Bumrah's last T20I was the T20 World Cup final against New Zealand in March; the series also doubles as preparation for the Asian Games later this month.

Full Tilt in the Nets

The most encouraging sight of India's training session at the Arun Jaitley Stadium on Thursday had nothing to do with a match. Jasprit Bumrah, back in Indian colours after two months on the sidelines with a left knee injury, ran in at full intensity and gave the batting unit — most notably 15-year-old sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi — a thorough working over. By every account from the session, the pace, rhythm and menace were all back.

The nets outing is the clearest evidence yet that Bumrah has taken another step on what an ESPNcricinfo report described as his road back to T20Is. The fast bowler has been out of action since India's ODI tour of England in July, when he sustained the injury while fielding during the second ODI in Cardiff on July 16. He was ruled out of the final ODI at Lord's and missed India's subsequent two-Test series in Sri Lanka, which the visitors won 1-0 without him.

"As a player comes out of an injury, it's important that he gets game time, and you need that sort of confidence when you're coming into the game."

— Shreyas Iyer, India captain

Iyer Backs His Spearhead

Speaking at his pre-series press conference, captain Shreyas Iyer made clear how India intends to manage its most valuable bowler. Game time, he said, is the priority — not caution for its own sake.

"He (Bumrah) has played so much cricket over the years, he's immensely experienced," Iyer said. "But at the end of the day, if you would ask me as an individual who's coming out of an injury, I would want more game time and more confidence leading up to a certain tournament."

That tournament is already in view. The selectors have named an identical 15-member squad for both the Afghanistan series and the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya later this month, with Bumrah's inclusion in both contingent on fitness clearance. His last appearance in the format came in the T20 World Cup final against New Zealand in March — an unusually long gap for a bowler who remains the reference point for fast bowling in the shortest format.

The Sooryavanshi Test

If Bumrah needed a barometer of his own sharpness, the nets provided a formidable one. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who arrived in the national camp after the Duleep Trophy final, is fresh off winning the IPL 2026 Orange Cap as the season's highest run-scorer — a 15-year-old who has been dismantling world-class attacks for two seasons. Reports from Thursday's session described Bumrah testing him hard, repeatedly placing the teenager in uncomfortable situations alongside the rest of India's pace group.

It is a sign of how quickly this Indian side is turning over that Bumrah and Sooryavanshi have never played a T20I together. The squad blending continues elsewhere too: Sanju Samson returns after missing the Zimbabwe tour in July, Varun Chakaravarthy is back in the setup, and Washington Sundar and Nitish Kumar Reddy are included subject to fitness clearance. Yash Thakur replaced Harshit Rana in the squad.

"If you look at Jasprit Bumrah, he is one of the best, and he is my favourite fast bowler. We as a group never think things in a complicated way for ourselves. So we have a very good plan for him."

— Ibrahim Zadran, Afghanistan captain

Afghanistan Ready With Plans

Afghanistan, the designated home team for the series despite all three matches being played in New Delhi, are treating Bumrah's return as the defining tactical challenge of the contest. Captain Ibrahim Zadran, who has taken over the T20I captaincy from Rashid Khan, told reporters on Saturday that his side has devised specific plans to counter the returning quick — and has done its homework on Sooryavanshi using IPL intelligence gathered from teammates who have faced him in 2025 and 2026.

"We have a very good plan for him, and we just thought about him, how to play against him, and hopefully we are going to play better cricket against Jasprit Bumrah or the Indian Cricket Team," Zadran said.

What's Next

The three T20Is are scheduled for September 13, 15 and 17 at the Arun Jaitley Stadium, with the opener at 7:30 PM IST on Sunday. Whether Bumrah plays all three will reveal how much of Iyer's "game time" philosophy the team management applies in practice. For a bowler whose workload has been the most debated topic in Indian cricket for years, the more immediate question is simpler: Thursday's nets suggested the knee is no longer the story. The cricket, at last, can be.
image_caption: Jasprit Bumrah. The pacer bowled at full intensity in the Delhi nets on Thursday as he closes in on a T20I return against Afghanistan.
nri_angle: Bumrah's injury comeback is the biggest storyline in Indian cricket for diaspora fans, and the Afghanistan series — played entirely in Delhi — offers a rare home-format tune-up before the Asian Games.
